# 两个随机变量独立是指它们取值所生成的任意事件都独立
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
*Two random variables are independent when every event generated by one is independent of every event generated by the other*
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->

> [!summary] 原子定义
> 随机变量 $X$ 与 $Y$ 独立，是指由 $X$ 的取值形成的每个事件，都与由 $Y$ 的取值形成的每个事件独立。对实值随机变量，这写成：任取 Borel 集 $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R$，
> $$P(X\in A,Y\in B)=P(X\in A)P(Y\in B).$$
> <!-- bilingual-en:start -->
> Random variables $X$ and $Y$ are independent when every event generated by the value of $X$ is independent of every event generated by the value of $Y$. For real-valued variables this means $P(X\in A,Y\in B)=P(X\in A)P(Y\in B)$ for all Borel sets $A,B$.
> <!-- bilingual-en:end -->

## 直觉
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
*Intuition*
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->

独立不是“两个数值看起来没有关系”，而是知道 $X$ 落在哪个集合里，不会改变 $Y$ 落入任意集合的概率。联合 CDF、PMF 或密度的计算判据单独见 [[随机变量独立的分布判据]]。
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
Independence does not mean that two numerical values merely look unrelated. It means that learning which set contains $X$ does not change the probability that $Y$ lies in any set. Computational tests using a joint CDF, PMF, or density are separated into [[随机变量独立的分布判据]].
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->

## 最小例子
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
*Minimal example*
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->

独立抛两枚公平硬币，令 $X,Y\in\{0,1\}$ 分别表示两枚硬币是否为正面。四种组合各以概率 $1/4$ 出现，因此任意 $x,y\in\{0,1\}$ 都有
$$P(X=x,Y=y)=\tfrac14=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=P(X=x)P(Y=y).$$
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
Toss two fair coins independently and let $X,Y\in\{0,1\}$ indicate heads. Each of the four pairs occurs with probability $1/4$, so $P(X=x,Y=y)=P(X=x)P(Y=y)$ for every possible pair.
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->

> [!question]- 自检
> 若对某些集合 $A,B$ 有 $P(X\in A,Y\in B)\neq P(X\in A)P(Y\in B)$，能否仍说 $X,Y$ 独立？
> <!-- bilingual-en:start -->
> If some sets $A,B$ violate $P(X\in A,Y\in B)=P(X\in A)P(Y\in B)$, can $X,Y$ still be independent?
> <!-- bilingual-en:end -->
>
> **答案：** 不能。定义要求所有由两变量取值形成的事件都满足乘积分解；一个反例就足以否定独立。
> <!-- bilingual-en:start -->
> **Answer:** No. The definition requires factorisation for every pair of events generated by the variables, so one counterexample disproves independence.
> <!-- bilingual-en:end -->

## 来源与核验

- [MIT 18.05 Reading 7a: Joint Distributions, Independence](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-05-introduction-to-probability-and-statistics-spring-2022/mit18_05_s22_class07-prep-a.pdf)，§4：支持以任意取值事件的乘积分解定义随机变量独立。
<!-- bilingual-en:start -->
- MIT 18.05 Reading 7a supports defining random-variable independence through factorisation of arbitrary events generated by the variables.
<!-- bilingual-en:end -->
